target_customer: Hospitals and health systems training and supporting frontline staff such as nurses
problem: Frontline hospital staff lack quick access to protocols and coaching at point of care; Elemeno delivers microlearning and communication on mobile.

founders.name: Arup Roy-Burman
founders.background_notes: Former pediatric ICU medical director at UCSF

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile content and communication platform; difficulty lay in hospital integration and security.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded in hospital workflows with customer content, but healthcare IT rivals could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found that incumbents copied or bought it.

market_need_then: Hospitals faced staff turnover and training burden; founder had direct ICU management experience and UCSF supported the product.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive but no press on brand, mascot or community found.

outcome_analysis: Elemeno, built by a UCSF pediatric ICU physician, raised a $1.3M seed in 2017 and a roughly $7M Series A in 2022 led by SJF Ventures, selling training and communication tools to hospitals. Slow healthcare sales cycles lengthened the path, but it remains active with later extensions reported.
notes: Series A amount from aggregators; Business Wire page returned 403 so unread. CB Insights reports extra Series A tranches in 2023 and 2024; unverified. Confidence stated high though competition is empty: none found near 2016, so medium would be stricter. Name origin not found.
